entries.title: I Samuel 23:2
segments: A conviction of our dependence on God, and a disposition to seek his direction, are a good preparation for receiving his favor and securing success.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:6
segments: An ephod in his hand; this is supposed to have been the high-priest's ephod, containing the breastplate with Urim and Thummim. Upon the death of Ahimelech this was saved by Abiathar in his flight, and David consulted God by it.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:7
segments: Men are apt to interpret the providences of God, and a disposition to seek his direction, are a good preparaton for receiving his favor and securing success.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:12
segments: It is not uncommon for men to return evil for good, and requite their benefactors with base ingratitude.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:14
segments: Wilderness of Ziph; a rough, hilly region in the tribe of Judah south-east of Hebron.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:16
segments:
Strengthened his hand in God; encouraged him to hope in God, and expect deliverance from him. 
 
Pious friendship delights in giving comfort in distress, by raising expectations from, and inspiring hope in Jehovah.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:21
segments: Men sometimes invoke the blessing of the Lord in the pursuit of objects which he abhors.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:24
segments: Maon; a place south of Ziph.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:27
segments: The Lord has a variety of ways in which he can protect his people, and he sometimes makes use of one enemy to deliver them from another.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:28
segments: Sela-hammah-lekoth; meaning, according to some interpreters, the rock of divisions; according to others, the rock of escape.

entries.title: I Samuel 23:29
segments: En-gedi; north-east of Maon, and on the border of the Dead sea; called also, Hazezon-tamar.
